proofs.locator: PDF page 2 / p.544, Proof of Theorem 1 and final known-L paragraph; equation (2) on p.543
map: The Proof begins with the smoothness descent estimate for y_k(α)=y_k−α∇f(y_k), explaining condition (4).
It defines p_k=(a_k−1)(x_{k−1}−x_k), expands the squared-distance change, and combines condition (4) with convexity.
Using a_{k+1}²−a_{k+1}=a_k² and nonincreasing α_k, the displayed chain bounds 2α_k a_k²(f(x_k)−f*) by ||y_0−x*||².
The source notes a_{k+1}≥a_k+0.5≥1+0.5(k+1). The final paragraph explicitly specializes α_k=1/L and replaces C by 2LR².
proofs.omitted_details: The source algebra is mapped rather than reproduced or independently certified. No local transfer theorem or correction to the printed NG formula is proposed.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually read the statement, definitions, displayed Proof chain and known-L paragraph on registered original-page images for printed pp.543–544. Page-labelled text was used for navigation. No whole-paper Proof review is claimed.

assumptions: For every x,y∈E, ||∇f(x)−∇f(y)||≤L||x−y||, with a known valid L>0.
X* is nonempty; y_0 is any point of E.
Use the exact stated recurrence with α_k=1/L, exact gradients and the initialization above.
statement.conclusion: f(x_k)−f*≤2LR²/(k+2)² for every integer k≥0. This is equation (6) with the final p.544 known-L substitution C=2LR²; no exact accuracy-to-query-count formula is included in this conclusion.
statement.objects_and_definitions: E is a Hilbert space, f:E→R is convex and continuously differentiable, X*=argmin_E f is nonempty, f*=min_E f, and R=||y_0−x*|| for a chosen x*∈X*. Define x_{−1}=y_0, a_0=1; for k≥0 define x_k=y_k−∇f(y_k)/L, a_{k+1}=(1+sqrt(4a_k²+1))/2 and y_{k+1}=x_k+((a_k−1)/a_{k+1})(x_k−x_{k−1}).
statement.parameter_domains: L∈(0,∞), k∈{0,1,2,…}, R=||y_0−x*||∈[0,∞). No strong-convexity assumption or finite-dimensional restriction is imposed in this statement.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such E,f,L,y_0, every minimizer x*∈X*, and every integer k≥0, the deterministic bound holds; there is no random choice or probability qualifier.
